patch.description: Partial edits applied to the current content, in order and atomically (one failing operation aborts the whole save). Every anchor string must match the current content exactly once. Only valid on update, in place of the full content/description field

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current content exactly once

new_string.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the match

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

anchor.description: Exact text to insert before. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly before the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")

anchor.description: Exact text to insert after. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly after the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")
Text to insert at the very start of the content
Text to insert at the very end of the content

from.description: Exact text where the range starts (inclusive). Must match exactly once

to.description: Exact text where the range ends (exclusive, stays in place). Must match exactly once after `from`

new_string.description: Text replacing the range. Empty string deletes it

team.description: Team name or ID (required when creating)

template.description: Template name or ID. Applied on create only. The template fills in the content, fields, and sub-issues server-side. A `description` replaces the template body rather than merging with it, but an empty `description` keeps the template body. Labels merge with the template's own

cycle.description: Cycle name, number, or ID. Null to remove

project.description: Project name, ID, identifier (e.g., P-ENG-123), or slug. Null to remove

assignee.description: User ID, name, email, or "me". Null to remove

delegate.description: Agent name or ID. When the user asks to delegate to "Linear" or "the Linear agent", this refers to the "Linear" app user specifically. Null to remove

labels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]). Replaces the full label set; existing labels not included are removed. Omit to leave labels unchanged. Cannot be combined with addLabels/removeLabels; prefer those for incremental changes

addLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to add. Append-only; existing labels are never removed. Cannot be combined with a team change

removeLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Urgent"]) to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue. Cannot be combined with a team change

dueDate.description: Due date (ISO format). On update, pass null to remove the due date

slaBreachesAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp when the SLA will breach. On update, pass null to remove the SLA

slaType.description: SLA day counting type: "all" or "onlyBusinessDays". Only use with slaBreachesAt; null means unset

parentId.description: Parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., LIN-123). Null to remove

estimate.description: Issue estimate value. On create, pass null or omit for no estimate. On update, pass null to clear the estimate; omitting leaves it unchanged. 0 is a real estimate only on teams that allow zero estimates.

links.description: Link attachments to add [{url, title}]. Append-only; existing links are never removed

setReleases.description: Replace all releases on the issue with these. Cannot be combined with addReleases/removeReleases

addReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to add. Append-only; existing releases are never removed

removeReleases.description: Release IDs or slugs to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue

blocks.description: Issue IDs/identifiers this blocks. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

blockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers blocking this. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

relatedTo.description: Related issue IDs/identifiers. Append-only; existing relations are never removed

duplicateOf.description: Duplicate of issue ID/identifier. Null to remove

removeBlockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers to remove as blockers of this issue

input.title: brain publish fails on a connected repo: "fact stream contains multiple branches" with no remedy
input.description:
Found in the 2026-10-20 state audit of every brain CLI command (connected / disconnected / local-only), binary built from main (631d91b4).

**Repro**

On the connected gh/entireio/entire-brain repo:

```
entire brain publish
```

**Observed**

```
publish: read facts require-cli-version-connect-9c2d9058: fact stream contains multiple branches
```

Exit 1. Publish on a healthy connected repo is broken for this brain.

**Problems**

1. Publish cannot serialize the local brain when a per-branch fact stream contains records from more than one branch. The local store got into this state through normal use (possibly related to the duplicate-memory-id corruption that `brief` warns about on this brain: 1315 repeated ids). Publish should either tolerate or repair this, or the writer that produced the mixed stream is the bug.
2. The message gives no remedy: no file path, no branch explanation, nothing to run next.

**Expected**

Publish succeeds, or fails with the offending store file and a concrete next step (e.g. `entire brain repair` / `refresh`).

input.title: brain connect exits 0 and prints "now syncing memories" when sync fails or ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS suppresses it
input.description:
Found in the 2026-10-20 state audit of every brain CLI command, binary built from main (631d91b4).

**Case 1 — initial sync fails**

On a repo with stored coordinates the server rejects (403):

```
+ Connected: repo 01SBXTEST00000000000000000 is now syncing memories

Memories sync periodically, at session end, and on git push. ...
hosted sync: branch main publish failed (local brain unaffected): factsync: POST facts:upsert ...: unexpected status 403 Forbidden: Forbidden; pull-only
hosted sync: branch main pull failed (local brain unaffected): factsync: GET facts feed ...: unexpected status 403 Forbidden: Forbidden
```

Exit 0. The headline and exit code contradict the sync result: both directions failed, nothing syncs.

**Case 2 — ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS=1**

`connect` writes the binding, prints the same "+ Connected: … is now syncing memories", silently skips the sync, exits 0. Nothing mentions that the kill switch suppresses everything the message just promised. (`disconnect` under no-egress is fine — it needs no egress.)

**Minor, same surface:** re-running `connect` on an already-connected repo also says "is now syncing memories" rather than acknowledging it was already connected.

**Expected**

- Case 1: non-zero exit or a headline that says connection recorded but verification failed.
- Case 2: an explicit line that ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS is set and nothing will sync until it is unset.

input.title: brain refresh hard-fails with cryptic checkpoint_scope_incomplete on repos with no checkpoints — but succeeds under no-egress
input.description:
Found in the 2026-10-20 state audit of every brain CLI command, binary built from main (631d91b4).

**Repro**

On a git repo where Entire has no readable checkpoints (e.g. Entire not enabled):

```
entire brain refresh            # also: refresh sessions, refresh delta
```

**Observed (egress allowed — connected or disconnected repo state)**

```
checkpoint_scope_incomplete: Entire returned no readable checkpoint IDs from an incomplete persistent-store inventory
```

Hard failure, exit 1. `patterns refresh` then fails ("session history missing"), and `doctor` reports the same error with the remedy "run `entire-brain setup`" — which fails the same way (circular).

**Observed (ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS=1, same repo)**

```
exported 0 sessions from 0 checkpoints
warning: no checkpoints have been captured in this repository yet
```

Exit 0.

**Cause**

`discoverCheckpoints` (internal/cli/export.go) shells to `entire checkpoint explain --json --search-all`; an incomplete inventory with zero checkpoint IDs becomes a hard error. The no-egress path skips routed discovery and reports the friendly zero-checkpoint result.

**Expected**

The two modes agree: zero checkpoints on a never-checkpointed repo is the normal empty case, not an error. The incomplete-inventory error, where still needed, should say what it means and what to do in plain words.

input.title: brain memories proposals list on a connected repo surfaces a raw 404 instead of "no proposals" / unsupported
input.description:
Found in the 2026-10-20 state audit of every brain CLI command, binary built from main (631d91b4).

**Repro**

On the connected gh/entireio/entire-brain repo:

```
entire brain memories proposals list
```

**Observed**

```
factsync: backend does not serve the open-proposal queue: GET proposals 01KWZ6252FA5XEMQJYDQ5ZX6RQ/brain-command-state-audit: 404 Not Found: not found
```

Exit 1.

**Problems**

- Internal jargon on the human surface: `factsync`, the HTTP verb, the raw coordinates.
- Doubled status text: "404 Not Found: not found".
- No remedy and no graceful handling: an empty or unsupported queue on a healthy connected repo should read like "no open proposals" or "this server does not serve the proposal queue", not a transport error.

Compare the disconnected and no-egress gates for the same command, which are clear one-liners.

input.title: brain memory retry/cancel/configure print machine telemetry receipts on the human surface
input.description:
Found in the 2026-10-20 state audit of every brain CLI command, binary built from main (631d91b4).

**Repro**

```
entire brain memory retry some-job-id
entire brain memory cancel some-job-id
entire brain memory configure abstracts --enable
```

**Observed**

```
retry failed schema_version=1 operation_id=op:ec775298240421cc dry_run=false error_code=memory_source_stale started_at=2026-10-21T05:44:27.133598Z finished_at=2026-10-21T05:44:27.134321Z artifacts=0 jobs=0
memory_source_stale: job bogus-job-id not found
```

`configure abstracts` additionally prints an artifact line (`artifact path="history/memory-config-v1.json" prior_state="absent" new_state="absent"`).

**Problem**

The receipt line (schema_version, operation_id, timestamps, counters) is machine telemetry. On the human surface only the last line matters ("job … not found" / "no abstract provider configured"). The receipt belongs behind `--json`.

**Expected**

Human output: the one-line result. Full receipt only with `--json`.

input.title: brain add: clone failure dumps git argv and duplicated raw git stderr
input.description:
Found in the 2026-10-20 state audit of every brain CLI command, binary built from main (631d91b4).

**Repro**

```
entire brain add https://github.com/sandbox-audit/nonexistent-repo.git
```

**Observed**

```
clone: https://github.com/sandbox-audit/nonexistent-repo.git -> sandbox-audit_nonexistent-repo
clone_failed: git [--no-optional-locks -c core.fsmonitor=false -c core.hooksPath=/dev/null/entire-brain-hooks-disabled clone --quiet -- https://github.com/sandbox-audit/nonexistent-repo.git sandbox-audit_nonexistent-repo]: exit status 128: remote: Repository not found.
fatal: repository 'https://github.com/sandbox-audit/nonexistent-repo.git/' not found
: remote: Repository not found.
fatal: repository 'https://github.com/sandbox-audit/nonexistent-repo.git/' not found
```

The full git argv, the git stderr printed twice, and a stray `: ` line.

**Expected**

One line: the URL and "repository not found (or no access)". The argv and raw stderr can live behind a verbose flag.

The no-egress gate for the same command is already right: `no_egress: add requires cloning or fetching repository history; unset ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS to allow it`.

input.title: brain connect placement error embeds raw host-CLI noise and a dangling clause
input.description:
Found in the 2026-10-20 state audit of every brain CLI command, binary built from main (631d91b4).

**Repro**

`entire brain connect` on a repo with no stored coordinates and no hosted placement (repo not visible from the login).

**Observed**

```
connect: resolve hosted placement (`entire repo view --json`): entire [repo view --json]: exit status 1: Using context 'us.auth.entire.io'.
no repo matching "sandbox-audit/brain-sbx" visible from your login (GitHub repos you could onboard: `entire repo mirror list --available`)
; pass --repo-id and --api-url explicitly
```

**Problems**

- Debug framing on the human surface: the backtick command, the argv echo (`entire [repo view --json]: exit status 1:`), the host CLI's "Using context …" banner.
- The embedded stderr's trailing newline leaves `; pass --repo-id and --api-url explicitly` dangling on its own line starting with `;`.

The useful content is already there (no matching repo, the mirror-list hint, the explicit-flags fallback) — it just needs clean framing.

**Expected**

Something like:

```
connect: no repo matching "sandbox-audit/brain-sbx" is visible from your login.
See onboardable repos: entire repo mirror list --available
Or pass --repo-id and --api-url explicitly.
```

input.title: brain distill --dry-run is blocked by ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS even though it spends nothing and does no egress
input.description:
Found in the 2026-10-20 state audit of every brain CLI command, binary built from main (631d91b4).

**Repro**

```
ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS=1 entire brain distill --dry-run
```

**Observed**

```
no_egress: --agent auto can send selected brain context outside local loopback; use --agent ollama for local loopback models, --agent none where supported, or unset ENTIRE_BRAIN_NO_EGRESS
```

Exit 1. The agent-egress gate fires on `--agent auto` before the dry-run short-circuit, but `--dry-run` is documented as "Estimate distill work without calling an agent or writing memories" — it needs no agent and no egress.

**Expected**

`distill --dry-run` works under no-egress. (The gate message itself is good — keep it for real runs.)

input.description:

```
entire brain privacy purge no-such-session-id
```

```
purged session no-such-session-id:
  0 derived index records
  derived store history/scan-cache.json.gz (51 bytes, rebuilds from surviving truth)
```

Exit 0. The session never existed, but the output says it was purged.

**Expected**

Say the id matched nothing, like `privacy exclude` already does:

```
excluded bogus-session-id: tombstone recorded, nothing to remove or rebuild
  no captured session in this brain matches this id
```

(Exit code choice — 0 with a clear "no match" line, or non-zero — just needs to be deliberate and consistent with exclude.)

input.title: Decide: should plain `memories sync` use the hosted backend on a connected repo?
input.description:
From the 2026-10-20 state audit of every brain CLI command, binary built from main (631d91b4).

On a connected repo, `entire brain memories sync` with no flags syncs via **local-gitmeta**:

```
synced 0 local memory(ies) on <branch> via local-gitmeta (…/gitmeta.git): no change; …
```

Hosted sync only runs with `--memories-backend=http` (which works and resolves its target from the binding, per COR-2143).

**Question**

Is local-gitmeta the intended default on a connected repo? Arguments both ways:

- Keep local default: background sync already covers hosted; a manual `memories sync` staying local is predictable and egress-free.
- Switch when connected: a user on a connected repo running `memories sync` probably means "sync with my team", and the current default silently does something else.

Either way the behavior should be documented in the command help (it currently doesn't say what the default backend is or that connectedness doesn't change it).

Decision + either a help-text fix or a default change.

# Systematic Debugging

## Overview

**Core principle:** ALWAYS find root cause before attempting fixes. Symptom fixes are failure.

**Violating the letter of this process is violating the spirit of debugging.**

## The Iron Law

```
NO FIXES WITHOUT ROOT CAUSE INVESTIGATION FIRST
```

If you haven't completed Phase 1, you cannot propose fixes.

## When to Use

Use for ANY technical issue:
- Test failures
- Bugs in production
- Unexpected behavior
- Performance problems
- Build failures
- Integration issues

**Use this ESPECIALLY when:**
- Under time pressure (emergencies make guessing tempting)
- "Just one quick fix" seems obvious
- You've already tried multiple fixes
- Previous fix didn't work
- You don't fully understand the issue

**Don't skip when:**
- Issue seems simple (simple bugs have root causes too)
- You're in a hurry (rushing guarantees rework)
- Manager wants it fixed NOW (systematic is faster than thrashing)

## The Four Phases

You MUST complete each phase before proceeding to the next.

### Phase 1: Root Cause Investigation

**BEFORE attempting ANY fix:**

1. **Read Error Messages Carefully**
   - Don't skip past errors or warnings
   - They often contain the exact solution
   - Read stack traces completely
   - Note line numbers, file paths, error codes

2. **Reproduce Consistently**
   - Can you trigger it reliably?
   - What are the exact steps?
   - Does it happen every time?
   - If not reproducible → gather more data, don't guess

3. **Check Recent Changes**
   - What changed that could cause this?
   - Git diff, recent commits
   - New dependencies, config changes
   - Environmental differences

4. **Gather Evidence in Multi-Component Systems**

   **WHEN system has multiple components (CI → build → signing, API → service → database):**

   **BEFORE proposing fixes, add diagnostic instrumentation:**
   ```
   For EACH component boundary:
     - Log what data enters component
     - Log what data exits component
     - Verify environment/config propagation
     - Check state at each layer

   Run once to gather evidence showing WHERE it breaks
   THEN analyze evidence to identify failing component
   THEN investigate that specific component
   ```

   **Example (multi-layer system):**
   ```bash
   # Layer 1: Workflow
   echo "=== Secrets available in workflow: ==="
   echo "IDENTITY: $([ -n "${IDENTITY:-}" ] && echo SET || echo UNSET)"

   # Layer 2: Build script
   echo "=== Env vars in build script: ==="
   printenv IDENTITY >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "IDENTITY in environment" || echo "IDENTITY not in environment"

   # Layer 3: Signing script
   echo "=== Keychain state: ==="
   security list-keychains
   security find-identity -v

   # Layer 4: Actual signing
   codesign --sign "$IDENTITY" --verbose=4 "$APP"
   ```

   **This reveals:** Which layer fails (secrets → workflow ✓, workflow → build ✗)

5. **Trace Data Flow**

   **WHEN error is deep in call stack:**

   See `root-cause-tracing.md` in this directory for the complete backward tracing technique.

   **Quick version:**
   - Where does bad value originate?
   - What called this with bad value?
   - Keep tracing up until you find the source
   - Fix at source, not at symptom

### Phase 2: Pattern Analysis

**Find the pattern before fixing:**

1. **Find Working Examples**
   - Locate similar working code in same codebase
   - What works that's similar to what's broken?

2. **Compare Against References**
   - If implementing pattern, read reference implementation COMPLETELY
   - Don't skim - read every line
   - Understand the pattern fully before applying

3. **Identify Differences**
   - What's different between working and broken?
   - List every difference, however small
   - Don't assume "that can't matter"

4. **Understand Dependencies**
   - What other components does this need?
   - What settings, config, environment?
   - What assumptions does it make?

### Phase 3: Hypothesis and Testing

**Scientific method:**

1. **Form Single Hypothesis**
   - State clearly: "I think X is the root cause because Y"
   - Write it down
   - Be specific, not vague

2. **Test Minimally**
   - Make the SMALLEST possible change to test hypothesis
   - One variable at a time
   - Don't fix multiple things at once

3. **Verify Before Continuing**
   - Did it work? Yes → Phase 4
   - Didn't work? Form NEW hypothesis
   - DON'T add more fixes on top

4. **When You Don't Know**
   - Say "I don't understand X"
   - Don't pretend to know
   - Ask for help
   - Research more

### Phase 4: Implementation

**Fix the root cause, not the symptom:**

1. **Create Failing Test Case**
   - Simplest possible reproduction
   - Automated test if possible
   - One-off test script if no framework
   - MUST have before fixing
   - Use the `superpowers:test-driven-development` skill for writing proper failing tests

2. **Implement Single Fix**
   - Address the root cause identified
   - ONE change at a time
   - No "while I'm here" improvements
   - No bundled refactoring

3. **Verify Fix**
   - Test passes now?
   - No other tests broken?
   - Issue actually resolved?
   - Use the `superpowers:verification-before-completion` skill before claiming success

4. **If Fix Doesn't Work**
   - STOP
   - Count: How many fixes have you tried?
   - If < 3: Return to Phase 1, re-analyze with new information
   - **If ≥ 3: STOP and question the architecture (step 5 below)**
   - DON'T attempt Fix #4 without architectural discussion

5. **If 3+ Fixes Failed: Question Architecture**

   **Pattern indicating architectural problem:**
   - Each fix reveals new shared state/coupling/problem in different place
   - Fixes require "massive refactoring" to implement
   - Each fix creates new symptoms elsewhere

   **STOP and question fundamentals:**
   - Is this pattern fundamentally sound?
   - Are we "sticking with it through sheer inertia"?
   - Should we refactor architecture vs. continue fixing symptoms?

   **Discuss with your human partner before attempting more fixes**

   This is NOT a failed hypothesis - this is a wrong architecture.

## Red Flags - STOP and Follow Process

If you catch yourself thinking:
- "Quick fix for now, investigate later"
- "Just try changing X and see if it works"
- "Add multiple changes, run tests"
- "Skip the test, I'll manually verify"
- "It's probably X, let me fix that"
- "I don't fully understand but this might work"
- "Pattern says X but I'll adapt it differently"
- "Here are the main problems: [lists fixes without investigation]"
- Proposing solutions before tracing data flow
- **"One more fix attempt" (when already tried 2+)**
- **Each fix reveals new problem in different place**

**ALL of these mean: STOP. Return to Phase 1.**

**If 3+ fixes failed:** Question the architecture (see Phase 4.5)

## your human partner's Signals You're Doing It Wrong

**Watch for these redirections:**
- "Is that not happening?" - You assumed without verifying
- "Will it show us...?" - You should have added evidence gathering
- "Stop guessing" - You're proposing fixes without understanding
- "Ultra-think this" - Question fundamentals, not just symptoms
- "We're stuck?" (frustrated) - Your approach isn't working

**When you see these:** STOP. Return to Phase 1.

## Common Rationalizations

| Excuse | Reality |
|--------|---------|
| "Issue is simple, don't need process" | Simple issues have root causes too. Process is fast for simple bugs. |
| "Emergency, no time for process" | Systematic debugging is FASTER than guess-and-check thrashing. |
| "Just try this first, then investigate" | First fix sets the pattern. Do it right from the start. |
| "I'll write test after confirming fix works" | Untested fixes don't stick. Test first proves it. |
| "Multiple fixes at once saves time" | Can't isolate what worked. Causes new bugs. |
| "Reference too long, I'll adapt the pattern" | Partial understanding guarantees bugs. Read it completely. |
| "I see the problem, let me fix it" | Seeing symptoms ≠ understanding root cause. |
| "One more fix attempt" (after 2+ failures) | 3+ failures = architectural problem. Question pattern, don't fix again. |

## Quick Reference

| Phase | Key Activities | Success Criteria |
|-------|---------------|------------------|
| **1. Root Cause** | Read errors, reproduce, check changes, gather evidence | Understand WHAT and WHY |
| **2. Pattern** | Find working examples, compare | Identify differences |
| **3. Hypothesis** | Form theory, test minimally | Confirmed or new hypothesis |
| **4. Implementation** | Create test, fix, verify | Bug resolved, tests pass |

## When Process Reveals "No Root Cause"

If systematic investigation reveals issue is truly environmental, timing-dependent, or external:

1. You've completed the process
2. Document what you investigated
3. Implement appropriate handling (retry, timeout, error message)
4. Add monitoring/logging for future investigation

**But:** 95% of "no root cause" cases are incomplete investigation.

## Supporting Techniques

These techniques are part of systematic debugging and available in this directory:

- **`root-cause-tracing.md`** - Trace bugs backward through call stack to find original trigger
- **`defense-in-depth.md`** - Add validation at multiple layers after finding root cause
- **`condition-based-waiting.md`** - Replace arbitrary timeouts with condition polling

content.text:
The fix is in and verified at the unit level; full-suite run is still going in the background — I'll commit and report once it comes back green.

**Status so far on COR-2201:**
- Root cause: `firstFactBranch` (publish.go) required every record in a branch store to share one branch, but hosted pull (COR-2126) deliberately rebuilds a branch store from the repo-wide feed — so any repo that pulled teammates' `main` facts on a feature branch couldn't publish.
- Fix: publish now recovers each stream's owner by re-deriving the directory name (`slug + sha256(branch)[:4]` is verifiable) from candidate branches — the records' branches plus the dir slug. Truly unresolvable streams still refuse, now with an error naming the directory and the branches found.
- Verified: new tests (`TestPublishAcceptsPulledCrossBranchFactStreams`, `TestPublishRefusesUnresolvableFactStream`) pass, and real-repo `publish` moves past the fact stage — it now fails only on this brain's size (~1.1 GB vs 260 MB hosted limit), a separate, well-formed error.

input.command:
git add internal/cli/publish.go internal/cli/publish_correctness_test.go && git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Resolve a fact stream's branch from its directory, not record purity (COR-2201)

Hosted pull (COR-2126) rebuilds a branch store from the repo-wide feed, so
after a sync on a feature branch the store legitimately carries teammates'
main facts. Publish still assumed every record in a stream shares one branch
and refused the whole publish with "fact stream contains multiple branches".

The directory name is verifiable (slug + hash of the full branch name), so
publish now recovers each stream's owner by re-deriving the directory from
candidate branches: every branch the records name, plus the directory's own
slug for stores holding only pulled foreign records. A stream no candidate
re-derives still refuses, and the error now names the directory and the
record branches instead of a bare invariant.

Residual gap, documented at the resolver: a store of only foreign records for
a branch whose name sanitizes lossily (e.g. "evis/x") stays unpublishable
until that branch distills or records a fact of its own.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -1
